_about: The one list of topics used on dafyomiinsights.com, for articles and stories. Style: Title Case, 1-5 words (shorter is better), the site's Ashkenazi transliteration (Shabbos, Berachos, Kesubah), 'and' not '&'. A topic is a subject: never a citation (Magen Avraham 147:5), a masechta or daf (they have their own pages), or a person (sages are on the Stories by Sage pages). 'aliases' are old or alternative names; they all point to the topic, so never add a new topic that is already someone's alias. 'retired' lists old tags that are not topics at all. Edit this file to add a topic; scripts/topics/check.mjs checks it.

subtopics.name: Humility and Torah Greatness
subtopics.description: The idea that a humble appearance or circumstances can foster humility of spirit and help one reach higher levels in Torah.

subtopics.name: Knowing You Are Humble

subtopics.name: Misplaced Humility
subtopics.description: When humility becomes a fault, such as failing to protest an injustice or to make a needed ruling because one feels unworthy.

subtopics.description: Moshe's admission to Aharon that he had heard but forgotten a law, and why the Gemara praises his honesty.

subtopics.description: The danger of feeling pleased when a colleague errs in Torah learning, and why sages prayed to avoid causing or feeling such joy.

subtopics.description: Why the first word of Sefer Vayikra is written with a small aleph, and its connection to Moshe Rabbeinu's humility.

topics.description: Gratitude to Hashem and to people.

subtopics.name: Birthday as a Day of Thanksgiving

subtopics.name: Gratitude to Those Who Protect Us
subtopics.description: The obligation to show appreciation to people who risk their lives for others, seen as a natural extension of thanking anyone who helps us.

subtopics.description: The difficulty and greatness of openly saying 'I was wrong,' contrasted with leaders who look for excuses instead of admitting error.

subtopics.description: Whether pledging large sums from dishonestly earned money can bring merit, and the warning that such gifts may not protect the giver.

subtopics.name: Falsifying Torah to Avoid Danger
subtopics.description: Whether one may misrepresent Jewish law, for example in a religious exemption letter, to escape a decree or mandate.

subtopics.description: The ideal of honoring a commitment one only decided on silently, illustrated by a merchant who kept to a price he had accepted in his mind.

subtopics.name: Unpaid Items Under the Shopping Cart

subtopics.description: The three areas in which a scrupulously honest scholar may say something untrue, such as out of humility or to protect a host.

subtopics.name: White Lies to Spare Feelings
subtopics.description: When altering the truth slightly is allowed in order to avoid hurting or insulting another person.

topics.name: Anger

subtopics.description: The idea that reacting calmly when someone spills wine, instead of becoming angry, brings blessing and prosperity into the home.

subtopics.description: The severity of lifting a hand to strike someone, even without hitting, including the label of rasha and the question of excommunication.

subtopics.name: Using Delays to Build Patience
subtopics.description: Treating waiting and inconvenience as a chance to work on patience rather than a source of frustration and anger.

subtopics.name: Never Speaking Lashon Hara
subtopics.description: The merit of guarding one's speech completely from gossip and slander, and the commitment it requires.

subtopics.name: Not Embarrassing Someone Being Punished
subtopics.description: The Torah's sensitivity to the dignity of even sinners and the wicked, ensuring they suffer no more shame than necessary.

subtopics.name: Praying for Others Instead of Criticizing
subtopics.description: The lesson from Hashem's rebuke of the prophet Hoshea that one should pray for people who sin rather than speak against them.

subtopics.name: Publicizing a Wrongdoer's Actions

subtopics.name: Lying for Shalom Bayis
subtopics.description: When changing the truth is permitted for the sake of peace in the home, and why habitual lying, even for peace, may be discouraged.

subtopics.name: Misjudging Others' Intentions
subtopics.description: How disputes arise when people misread one another's feelings and motives, as seen with Yosef and his brothers.

topics.name: Avodah Zarah
topics.description: Idolatry and its prohibitions, from images and statues to bowing.

subtopics.name: Aharon and the Golden Calf
subtopics.description: Explanations of why Aharon helped make the Golden Calf, including the view that he hoped to prevent a worse sin, and whether this was right.

subtopics.name: Bowing to an Official Wearing Idols
subtopics.description: Whether a Jew may bow to a ruler who wears idolatrous images or claims divinity, and why Mordechai refused to bow to Haman.

subtopics.name: Church Bells and Church Clocks
subtopics.description: Whether one may listen to church music or use a church clock to tell the time, given the prohibition on benefiting from idolatry.

subtopics.name: Coins With a Human Face
subtopics.description: Whether making a raised image of a person, such as a portrait on a coin or medal, is forbidden while flat drawings are allowed.

subtopics.name: Destruction of the Copper Snake
subtopics.description: Why the copper snake Moshe made was preserved for centuries and later destroyed by Chizkiyahu once people began worshipping it.

subtopics.name: Drawing the Sun and Moon
subtopics.description: Whether one may draw or depict the sun, moon, stars and zodiac signs, and whether two-dimensional drawings or children's art are permitted.
aliases: Drawing Pictures of the Sun and Moon
Children Drawing Pictures of the Sun
Children Drawing the Sun and Moon

subtopics.name: Making Sculptures of People
subtopics.description: The prohibition on fashioning raised images of a human form, such as a portrait on a coin, and why flat drawings are treated differently.

subtopics.name: Pictures of the Moon in Textbooks
subtopics.description: Whether owning books or magazines that contain images of the moon is a concern today, given the reason behind the original rule.

subtopics.name: Roman Emperors' Birthdays as Festivals
subtopics.description: The Gemara's listing of rulers' birthdays among idolatrous festivals, and the restrictions on doing business around those days.

subtopics.name: Worshipped Water Sources
subtopics.description: Why public water worshipped by idolaters stays permitted for drinking while a privately owned water source may become forbidden.

subtopics.name: Worshipping Idols Out of Fear
subtopics.description: Whether an act of idol worship done out of fear or respect for a person counts as idolatry, and when one must give up one's life instead.

topics.name: Medicine and Health
topics.description: Healing, doctors, pikuach nefesh and the Gemara's health advice.

subtopics.name: Choosing the Lesser Melacha in an Emergency
subtopics.description: The principle of minimizing the severity of Shabbos violations in non-life-threatening medical situations, as taught to Hatzalah members.

subtopics.name: Doctors Charging for Medical Care
subtopics.description: Whether a doctor may charge for healing when it is considered a mitzvah, compared with returning a lost object.

subtopics.name: Donating Blood for a Patient
subtopics.description: Organizing blood donations credited to a sick person, and finding other ways to help when one cannot donate.

subtopics.name: Easing a Patient's Mind on Shabbos
subtopics.description: How concern for a sick person's peace of mind, even short of mortal danger, can affect what is allowed on Shabbos.

subtopics.name: Exceptions to Pikuach Nefesh
subtopics.description: Prohibitions beyond the three cardinal sins that may not be overridden even to save a life, such as public shaming.

subtopics.name: How Long Can a Person Stay Awake
subtopics.description: The limits of human wakefulness, record attempts to stay awake, and how microsleep explains apparent feats beyond three days.

subtopics.name: Medicines From Non-Kosher Animals
subtopics.description: The status of animal-derived products such as horse urine used in hormone drugs, and how the Rishonim rule on them.

subtopics.name: Overeating and Health
subtopics.description: Talmudic and medieval advice to stop eating before one is full, the link between overeating and illness, and its value as spiritual discipline.

subtopics.name: Remote Danger and Pikuach Nefesh
subtopics.description: How unlikely a threat to life must be before it no longer justifies breaking Shabbos or another prohibition, and whether present danger differs from future danger.

subtopics.name: Saving a Mother in Dangerous Childbirth
subtopics.description: The halachic rules when a baby endangers its mother during birth, and why the law changes once the baby is partly born.

subtopics.name: Surgical Skin Markings
subtopics.description: Whether doctors may mark a patient's skin before surgery to identify the correct site, in light of the prohibition of tattooing.

subtopics.name: Thermometer Strips on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether a forehead strip that shows temperature by changing color may be used on Shabbos, and for whom it may be allowed.

subtopics.name: Two Travelers With One Canteen
subtopics.description: The Talmudic dilemma of two travelers with enough water for only one, and the ruling that one's own life comes first.

subtopics.name: Vaccines on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether Shabbos may be broken to receive a vaccine, depending on how likely a short delay is to put someone in danger.

subtopics.name: Walking After Eating
subtopics.description: The Talmudic health advice to walk a few steps after a meal before sleeping, and how it shaped what a creditor must leave a debtor.

topics.name: Aveilus
topics.description: Mourning, kevurah and honoring the dead.

subtopics.name: Burial of Jews With Tattoos
subtopics.description: The common belief that a Jew with a tattoo cannot be buried in a Jewish cemetery, and why it has no basis in Jewish law.

subtopics.name: Saying HaMakom Yenachem
subtopics.description: The meaning of the traditional words of comfort said to mourners and whether saying them alone fulfills the mitzvah of comforting mourners.

subtopics.name: Shemuah Rechokah
subtopics.description: The mourning rules for someone who learns of a relative's death more than thirty days after it happened.

subtopics.name: Telling Someone a Relative Died
subtopics.description: Whether one must inform a person that a close relative passed away, and how bad news should be shared.

subtopics.name: Waiting for the Mourner to Speak First
subtopics.description: The rule that visitors at a shivah house should not speak until the mourner begins, and how it fits with common practice.

subtopics.name: Yahrzeit in a Leap Year
subtopics.description: When to observe a parent's yahrzeit that fell in Adar of a regular year once a leap year with two Adars arrives.

topics.name: Gedolim
topics.description: Tributes, hespedim and stories about the great rabbanim of our time.

subtopics.name: Misinterpreting the Actions of Gedolim
subtopics.description: How casual actions or clever remarks of great rabbis are sometimes misunderstood and spread as binding halachic rulings.

topics.name: Technology and Halacha
topics.description: Modern technology through the lens of the Gemara: machines, voice devices, self-driving cars and more.

subtopics.name: Opening the Freezer on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether opening a fridge or freezer door on Shabbos is a problem because the warm air causes the compressor to turn on sooner.

subtopics.name: Self-Driving Cars on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether a voice-controlled or self-driving car could be used in a Shabbos emergency, and the rabbinic concerns that may still remain.

subtopics.name: Texting on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether typing on a phone or computer counts as the melacha of writing on Shabbos, and how screen savers affect whether the writing lasts.

subtopics.name: Voice-Activated Devices on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Whether speaking to a phone, computer or smart device that then performs a melacha counts as doing the melacha yourself on Shabbos.

topics.name: Jewish History
topics.description: Events and eras of Jewish history connected to the daf.

subtopics.name: 1848 Cholera Yom Kippur in Vilna
subtopics.description: The story of the Vilna cholera epidemic, when the community was told to eat on Yom Kippur, and the debate over what actually happened.

subtopics.name: Burial of the Beitar Victims
subtopics.description: The massacre at Beitar, the delayed burial of its victims, and the miracle remembered on Tu B'Av.

subtopics.name: Derech HaOfel Road History
subtopics.description: How a road built around the Old City of Yerushalayim for a 1964 papal visit later served Israeli soldiers and Torah students.

subtopics.name: Granada Massacre of 1066
subtopics.description: The killing of the Jewish community of Granada on the ninth of Teves, the first known massacre of Jews in Muslim Spain.

subtopics.name: Jewish Military Chaplains
subtopics.description: The work of rabbis serving Jewish soldiers on military bases, including running services, building a sukkah and countering missionary pressure.

subtopics.name: Mir Yeshiva Escape During the Holocaust
subtopics.description: How yeshiva students fled with the Mir Yeshiva through Japan and China and survived the Holocaust while many who stayed behind perished.

subtopics.name: Napoleon Cloak Story
subtopics.description: The account of a Jew in Mogilev who helped the retreating emperor in 1812 and received his cloak, later made into a paroches.

subtopics.name: Pope's 1964 Visit to Israel
subtopics.description: The first papal visit to Israel in 1964, and how a road built for that trip later played a role in reuniting Jerusalem in 1967.

subtopics.name: Slavuta Shas and Vilna Shas Dispute
subtopics.description: The nineteenth-century rivalry between the Slavuta and Romm printers over publishing rights to the Talmud, and the bitter controversy and tragedy it caused.

subtopics.name: Spies Generation Dying in the Desert
subtopics.description: The decree that the generation of the spies would die in the wilderness, and the yearly Tishah B'Av deaths that ended on Tu B'Av.

subtopics.name: Tosfos Written Before Martyrdom
subtopics.description: The tradition that two long Tosfos commentaries were composed by sages on the night before their execution for refusing to convert.

subtopics.name: Translation of the Torah Into Greek
subtopics.description: Why the miraculous translation of the Torah into Greek for King Ptolemy is remembered as a sad day for the Jewish people.

topics.name: Eretz Yisrael
topics.description: The Land of Israel: living there, its holiness and its boundaries.

subtopics.name: Dividing Eretz Yisrael by Lottery
subtopics.description: How Yehoshua divided the land among the tribes by lot at Gilgal and Shiloh, and which tribes took part in each stage.

subtopics.name: Learning Torah in Eretz Yisrael
subtopics.description: Whether the spiritual advantage of studying Torah in the Land of Israel outweighs the loss of a suitable study partner.

subtopics.name: Making Aliyah on Yom Tov Sheni
subtopics.description: Whether people arriving to settle in Israel on the second day of a festival must keep that day or stop observing it.
aliases: Moving to Israel During Yom Tov
Making Aliyah During Yom Tov Sheni

subtopics.name: Meaning of Me'aras HaMachpelah
subtopics.description: Two explanations of why the burial cave of the Avos is called "the doubled cave," and a practical difference for property contracts.

subtopics.name: Owning Land in Eretz Yisrael
subtopics.description: The idea that every Jewish family holds an ancestral share in the Land of Israel, and the halachic effects this may have.

subtopics.name: Reunification of Jerusalem in 1967
subtopics.description: How events and infrastructure in the years before the Six-Day War set the stage for Jerusalem's Old City coming under Jewish control.

topics.name: Non-Jews
topics.description: Relations with non-Jews, the Noahide laws and converts.

subtopics.name: Answering Christian Virgin Birth Claims
subtopics.description: How the Gemara's mention of Shimshon's sister has been used to answer claims of a fatherless birth and the lineage from Dovid.

subtopics.name: Convert Is Like a Newborn
subtopics.description: The principle that a person who converts to Judaism is considered newly born, and its halachic consequences.

subtopics.name: Converts From Amalek
subtopics.description: Whether a descendant of Amalek may convert to Judaism, the sources for and against, and how Haman's descendants came to teach Torah.

subtopics.name: Converts in Positions of Leadership
subtopics.description: The rule that converts are not normally appointed to positions of authority, and how great converted sages could still lead.

subtopics.name: Ger Toshav Before Conversion
subtopics.description: The status of a non-Jew who accepts the seven Noahide laws, and whether it can serve as a step toward full conversion.

subtopics.name: Moabite Converts and Dovid's Lineage
subtopics.description: The ruling that the ban on Moabite converts applies only to men and not women, which settled the question of Dovid HaMelech's descent from Rus.

topics.name: Animals
topics.description: Animals in halacha and aggadah, and tzaar baalei chaim.

subtopics.name: Feeding Stray Dogs on Shabbos
subtopics.description: Why feeding wild dogs on Shabbos is an exception to the rule against feeding animals that are not one's own.

subtopics.name: Muzzling Animals to Prevent Theft
subtopics.description: Muzzling work animals so they do not graze in other people's fields, and why even a tzaddik's animals were muzzled.

subtopics.name: Understanding the Speech of Trees
subtopics.description: The Talmudic report that a sage understood the speech of trees, and the different ways commentators explain it.

subtopics.name: Vegetarianism in Judaism
subtopics.description: How Jewish thought views animal rights and vegetarianism, and why compassion for animals does not necessarily mean avoiding meat.

topics.name: Travel
topics.description: Halacha on the road and in the air: davening, Tefillas HaDerech and travel questions.

subtopics.name: Adding Personal Requests to Tefillas HaDerech
subtopics.description: Whether a traveler may add specific requests, like protection from accidents, to the wayfarer's prayer, and whether to say it oneself.

subtopics.name: Crossing the Date Line During Sefirah
subtopics.description: How a traveler who skips or gains a day by crossing the international date line should continue counting the Omer.

subtopics.name: Davening on an Airplane
subtopics.description: Whether to stand or sit for Shemoneh Esrei on a plane, and concerns about blocking aisles and bathrooms for other passengers.

subtopics.name: Davening While Driving
subtopics.description: Whether a person may daven while driving a car, comparing it to the Gemara's permission to daven while riding a donkey.

subtopics.name: Emergency Landing for a Sick Passenger
subtopics.description: When a medical emergency on board justifies diverting a flight, weighing the patient's risk against the inconvenience to other passengers.

subtopics.name: Saying Tefillas HaDerech After Another Bracha
subtopics.description: Why Tefillas HaDerech lacks an opening Baruch Atah, and the practice of reciting another bracha such as Asher Yatzar right before it.
aliases: Saying a Berachah Before Tefillas HaDerech

subtopics.name: When to Say Tefillas HaDerech
subtopics.description: Which kinds of trips call for reciting the traveler's prayer, and why people on the same train or bus may differ in practice.

topics.name: Daf Quiz
topics.description: Test yourself: quizzes on the Daf Yomi.

topics.name: Rodeif
topics.description: A pursuer, self-defense and when one may stop an attacker.

subtopics.name: Is an Unwitting Attacker a Rodef
subtopics.description: Whether someone who unknowingly endangers others, such as a misinformed pilot, has the status of a pursuer who may be stopped by force.

subtopics.name: Sacrificing One Life to Save Many
subtopics.description: Whether it is ever permitted to take one innocent life in order to save several others, explored through a wartime rescue dilemma.
